title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Ops & Top Issues
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page defines standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operations, and the top support issues we see in the field. It is intended for DevEx writers, SDK owners, and on-call engineers who maintain public docs and quickstarts.

Scope
- SDK guides (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and starter templates for common workflows (text-generation, chat, embeddings, streaming)
- API examples and idiomatic usage patterns (sync, streaming, function-calling)
- Docs site operating procedures: PR process, release cadences, tagging and versioning
- Canonical fixes for top support issues and playbook for triage

Ownership and Contacts
- Owner team: engineering (DevEx team)
- Primary doc owner: Sofia Patel (DevEx Lead)
- Secondary owners: SDK maintainers (see per-language owners in the "Files & Templates" section)
- On-call escalation: eng-developer-experience on-call; pager: #devex-oncall

Doc Types and Templates (Quick reference)
- SDK Guide template: "sdk-guide-template.md" (sections: Overview, Install, Quickstart, API reference snippets, Common errors, Migration notes)
- Quickstart template: "quickstart-template.md" (1-page, 10-minute flow, config table, expected output)
- API Example recipe: "api-example-recipe.md" (pattern, sync/async variant, error handling)
- Release note template: "docs-release-note.md"

Standards for SDK Guides
- Language parity: Every public API must have examples in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript. Go/Java support must cover key paths (auth, basic request, streaming).
- Example sizes: Keep examples to 15-40 lines. Provide a runnable gist or sandbox where practical.
- Installation & versioning: Provide pip/npm/go module install line and a compatibility table:

Compatibility table (example):
| SDK | Min Version | Supported Models/Notes |
|-----|-------------|------------------------|
| python | 0.12.0 | text/chat/embeddings, streaming supported |
| js | 1.4.0 | text/chat/embeddings, function-calls example |

- Auth & config: Show environment-variable-based auth + explicit client construction. Example (Python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-1.1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Hello'}])
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates
- Purpose: 1-page guided flows that get a developer from zero to an observable result in ~10 minutes. Each quickstart contains: prerequisites, step-by-step commands, expected output, troubleshooting tips, and links to deeper docs.
- Required quickstarts (minimum set for any new SDK release):
  1. Hello world (token generation / chat)
  2. Streaming response example (client-side handling)
  3. Embeddings and similarity search (with a small dataset)
  4. Tool calling / function-calls pattern
  5. Deployment pattern: switching between hosted and dedicated endpoints

Example quickstart flow (Embeddings):
1) Prereqs: python 3.10+, pip install redwood-sdk>=0.12.0
2) Create dataset (local CSV) and run the embed command: `python examples/embeddings_create.py --file sample.csv`
3) Run nearest-neighbor lookup: `python examples/embeddings_query.py --q 'recipe for apple pie'`
4) Expected output: top-3 similar texts with confidence scores

Docs Site Operating Procedures
- Branching and PRs
  - All doc changes open a PR against `main-docs`. Small fixes (typos, broken links) can be merged by the DevEx owner after review.
  - Major changes (API surface, breaking example changes) require 2 reviewers: one DevEx writer and one SDK owner.
- Release cadence
  - Minor updates: merged to main-docs and deployed via netlify on merge (auto-deploy).
  - SDK or API version changes: coordinate with SDK lead and runtime release; schedule doc release the same day as public API rollout.
- Tagging and change logs
  - Every PR that changes examples must include `has-example-changes: true` label.
  - Add a short entry to the docs release note template describing the change and any migration steps.
- Monitoring and alerts
  - Broken link checks run nightly. Keep <1% broken-link rate across the docs site.
  - Examples failing CI (sandbox run) trigger an alert to #devex-ci with priority P2.

API Examples: Patterns and Best Practices
- Auth patterns: show env var + explicit token examples. Note: never embed real API keys in examples. Use placeholders: `REDACTED_API_KEY`
- Streaming examples: include both client and server-side handling for chunked responses (JS and Python).
- Function-calling/tooling: provide a canonical example for tools that mirrors production usage (validate JSON schema, fallback behavior).
- Error handling: always show how to parse error codes and retry safely with exponential backoff. Example shell for retries:
```bash
# Basic backoff pseudocode
for i in 1..5; do
  resp=$(curl -sS ... )
  status=$?
  if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then break; fi
  sleep $((2**i))
done
```

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (last 12 months)
- Summary: The following table lists the highest-frequency support issues we see reported against docs / quickstarts and the canonical fixes that should be applied to the docs and SDKs.

| ID | Symptom | Root cause | Canonical fix | Rollback / Mitigation | Owner |
|----|---------|------------|---------------|-----------------------|-------|
| S-101 | Quickstart streaming example raises JSONDecodeError | Example uses non-streaming response body parsing | Update example to use streaming iterator and add test in examples CI | Revert to previous doc and link to "known issue" note | SDK Team (Python) |
| S-102 | Embedding semantic search returns low-quality matches | Default vectorizer param mismatch for small corpora | Add recommended preprocessing step and tuned params in quickstart; include sample notebook | Add a note to quickstart to use `--sample-size 100` for small datasets | DevEx/Data-Science |
| S-103 | Auth failures in CI for examples | Missing instructions for setting REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI env | Add CI section to quickstart and example GitHub Actions workflow snippet | Add mock-mode examples and update CI to set `REDACTED_API_KEY` | DevEx / SDK owners |
| S-104 | API example uses deprecated parameter (timeout_ms) | API parameter renamed in runtime v1.3 | Update example to new parameter (timeout_ms -> timeout_seconds) and add ADR link | Provide compatibility note and example showing both parameters | API Platform Team |

Canonical fixes should include:
- Code change in SDK (if necessary) with a linked PR
- Doc update with example and migration note
- Add a unit/e2e example to examples CI that reproduces the issue and prevents regression
- Add an entry to `known-issues.md` if full fix is delayed

Runbook: Triage a Docs-related Support Ticket
1) Reproduce locally using the steps in the ticket (use the exact SDK version noted).
2) If reproduction fails, ask the reporter for logs and exact commands; request a minimal repro.
3) Check related CI for examples and run the relevant example.
4) If the issue is caused by the docs example, open a docs PR with a failing test or repro and tag `devex-triage`.
5) If the issue is caused by an SDK bug, open an SDK issue and reference the docs PR; the fix must include an example and passing example CI.

Metrics and SLOs for DevEx Docs
- Example-run CI pass rate: target >= 99% per release (daily report).
- Broken link rate: target < 1% (daily check).
- Doc freshness: every API example must be reviewed on runtime releases (v-major/minor); assign a review within 7 days of runtime release.
- Mean time to author fix for top-5 issues: <= 5 business days.

Release checklist for doc changes that affect examples or SDKs (numbered steps)
1. Open PR against `main-docs` or SDK repo with description and links to failing repro.
2. Add reviewers: 1 DevEx + 1 SDK owner.
3. Add label `has-example-changes: true` and `ci/sandbox: required` if the change includes runnable examples.
4. Update docs release note template with migration steps.
5. Ensure examples CI (sandbox) passes.
6. Merge and verify netlify deployment; run smoke test on the deployed page (link posted to #devex-ci).
7. Close related support ticket with links to PR and deployed page.

Appendices
A) Example GitHub Actions snippet (CI) to run examples (simplified):
```yaml
name: examples-ci
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  run-examples:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Install SDK
        run: pip install -e ./sdk/python
      - name: Run examples
        run: python examples/ci_run_all.py
        env:
          REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
```

B) Example contact matrix
- DevEx (doc changes, merging): Sofia Patel (devex@redwood.example.com)
- SDK owners (language-specific): see owners table in repo root
- Runtime/API changes: API Platform Team (api-platform@redwood.example.com)

C) Frequently referenced pages
- SDK repo README (per-language)
- examples/ directory with runnable quickstarts (linked from each guide)
- known-issues.md

Notes and next steps
- Action item: implement nightly example-run coverage report and post to #devex-metrics by 2026-04-01.
- Action item: expand quickstarts to include a server-side example for function-calling by Q2 2026.
